result.summary:
Independently re-derived all 7 acceptance criteria from docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-071 entry (read verbatim, not from any handoff's paraphrase) against the actual code/tests/docs on feature/WF02-REQ071-20260821 (commit 0e5df58 at start of this check).

AC1 (no Authorization header -> 401, zero Repo queries): read test/letflow/router_test.exs's 'REQ-071 AC1' describe block -- it attaches a named telemetry handler on [:letflow, :repo, :query] filtered to self()==test_pid (matching tenant_status_test.exs's ISS-0031 precedent, not an unfiltered send/2), asserts conn.status==401 and body['error']=='unauthorized', then refute_received :query_fired. Re-ran directly (mix test test/letflow/router_test.exs): 17 passed, 0 failures. AC1 genuinely met.

AC2 (valid token reaches handler, auth_context populated, end-to-end): read test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs's 'REQ-071 AC2' test. It goes through the real Letflow.Router.call/2 (not the plug in isolation), asserts conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id/roles/user_id are populated, and the request reaches :dispatch (proven by getting the stub sub-router's own 404 rather than a 401/403/500/503 from an earlier plug in the chain). My own independent judgment: this is not actually a substitution requiring a judgment call -- REQ-070's stub sub-router's match-all handler IS 'the handler' for this route today; AC2 says 'reaches the handler with auth_context populated', and it demonstrably does, through the real router. Re-ran directly (mix test test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs): 4 passed, 0 failures. AC2 genuinely met.

AC3 (GET /health 200 while OIDC worker down): re-ran test/letflow/router_test.exs's 'REQ-071 AC3' test directly. Confirmed it resolves the real Process.whereis(Letflow.Oidc.DefaultProvider), asserts is_pid, kills it with Process.exit(pid,:kill), waits on a real Process.monitor DOWN message, confirms not Process.alive?, then asserts GET /health still returns 200. This is a real kill of a real supervised process, not a stub. Passed. AC3 genuinely met.

AC4 (migrating POST -> 503+Retry-After; equivalent GET -> 200): the POST-half test is literal and passed (503, retry-after: 30, error: tenant_migrating). The GET-half substitutes 'not rejected (no 503/Retry-After), reaches the stub's own 404, TenantStatus's method short-circuit takes no Repo path for GET' for a literal 200. My own independent judgment, not inherited from CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's prior agreement: this substitution is legitimate. A literal 200 is structurally impossible right now without a real production route -- every /api/v1/* sub-router is REQ-070's stub whose only match clause returns not_found, and inventing a fake route to manufacture a literal 200 would be out-of-scope scope creep for a plug-mounting requirement. The substituted assertions (no 503, no Retry-After, reaches dispatch, TenantStatus's own write-gate query never fires for GET per tenant_status.ex's method allowlist) prove exactly what a literal 200 would have proven -- that TenantStatus's write-pause logic is scoped to write methods only. Re-ran directly: both AC4 tests passed (2 tests, part of the 4 in api_pipeline_integration_test.exs above). AC4 genuinely met given the structural constraint, and I independently agree with, not merely cite, the prior gates' reasoning here.

AC5 (concurrent tenant-status isolation, INV-8): read test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs's AC5 test. Confirmed genuine concurrency: bad_task = Task.async(...) is created and returned BEFORE good_task = Task.async(...) is created -- both Task.async calls fire before either is awaited (Task.await is only called after both async calls), so the bad (malformed tenant_id) and good (valid tenant) requests genuinely run concurrently, not sequentially. Confirmed the fail-closed crash: TenantStatus.call/2's check_write_pause/2 path does Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id) with a malformed (non-UUID) tenant_id and no try/rescue/with-guard anywhere in lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex around that call (read the file in full) -- it genuinely raises Ecto.Query.CastError, which the test only catches inside its own task body (to inspect the exception, not to prevent a crash) via {:crashed, e}. Confirmed isolation: the good task's conn is unaffected (not halted, status nil meaning it passed straight through TenantStatus without being touched by the bad task's exception) -- the two run in separate BEAM processes (Task.async spawns a linked-but-independent process; only Task.await propagates a failure to the caller, and the bad task's failure was caught inside its own process, never propagated). Re-ran directly: this test passed as part of the 4 in api_pipeline_integration_test.exs. AC5 genuinely met.

AC6 (moduledoc phrase removed): ran `grep -n "Not mounted in front of any route today" lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex` myself -- zero matches (exit code 0 from grep, no output lines). Also read lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex directly and confirmed the mounting: plug(Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline) then plug(Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus), both ahead of plug(:match)/plug(:dispatch), matching the required AuthPipeline-then-TenantStatus ordering from the requirement's description. AC6 genuinely met.

AC7 (REVIEWER's OQ-14 confirmation recorded in stage-4-api-surface.md): read docs/migration/stage-4-api-surface.md's '## REVIEWER sign-off' section (line 221) in full. Found a genuine, dated '2026-08-21 (REQ-071) -- PASS' entry (starting line 302) with real, checkable reasoning: quotes the exact tenant_status.ex line (59) where the un-rescued Repo.get call lives, names the deliberate divergence from R-Co's tenant_status.zig fail-open behavior, gives a substantive tradeoff argument (not a rubber stamp), confirms supervision integrity (:one_for_one, only the one Bandit request process dies), confirms Test 3's OIDC-worker-restart mechanics by reading application.ex directly, and states a scope check against git diff. This is not a stub entry. AC7 genuinely met.

FULL SUITE RE-RUN, independently, not trusted from TEST-RUNNER's report alone: first attempted via Monitor (background), corrected after ORCH pointed out subagents cannot receive cross-turn Monitor notifications (core-directives.md's 'No Background Wait For A Cross-Turn Notification') -- re-ran synchronously in the foreground instead. An initial N=16 (nproc-auto-derived) attempt reproduced the same environment-sizing problem TEST-RUNNER already filed as ISS-0219 (partitions crashing on DBConnection.ConnectionError/build-lock contention before any Result: line) -- confirms ISS-0219 is real and reproducible, not a one-off. Switched to TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 per TEST-RUNNER's own established working value for this host. A first TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 attempt (immediately following the N=16 attempt, itself right after Postgres had also just serviced this run's own earlier manual REQ-071-file-only test invocations) hit a transient 'too_many_connections'/connection-not-available failure in partition 3 (0 tests, crashed during ecto.migrate) -- checked `docker exec letflow-postgres-1 psql -U letflow -d postgres -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity'` (6 of max_connections=100) and `ps aux` for orphaned erl/beam processes (none found) immediately after, confirming the DB was clear and no leaked processes were holding connections -- i.e. it was genuine transient contention from back-to-back suite launches on this host, not a persistent leak. Re-ran once more, cleanly, with nothing else concurrent: TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh completed with combined: 1439 tests, 5 properties, 0 failures (1444/1444 passed) -- exit code 0, every one of the 4 partitions reporting 0 failures. This is BETTER than TEST-RUNNER's own Step 4 report (1428/1444, 16 failures), which reinforces rather than contradicts TEST-RUNNER's Route 1 attribution: the same 16 tests (Letflow.SandboxPoolTest, Letflow.SandboxPool.FixtureLoaderTest, Letflow.Definitions.PromotionAssertionRerunTest) that failed under TEST-RUNNER's run now pass cleanly under mine, consistent with the documented mechanism (SandboxPool claim-timeout resource contention, filed as ISS-0220) being genuinely load-dependent/environmental rather than a real regression -- a failure that disappears entirely under lighter concurrent load is the opposite signature of a real code defect, and confirms core-directives.md's own point that this suite's failure set varies run to run and must not be judged by count-matching in either direction. Independently re-ran `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` myself and confirmed none of the 5 SandboxPool/FixtureLoader/PromotionAssertionRerun-related files (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs, test/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex) appear in the diff -- Route 1 independently confirmed, not copied from ISS-0219/ISS-0220's text. Also directly re-ran REQ-071's own two test files in isolation (mix test test/letflow/router_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs): 21 passed, 0 failures, matching TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step 3b count.

VERDICT: PASS. All 7 acceptance criteria independently confirmed met against the actual code/tests/docs, not against any prior gate's narrative. Full suite re-run by me twice (once contaminated by back-to-back launches, corrected and re-run cleanly) confirms 1444/1444 passing with zero failures in the clean run -- stronger evidence than a PARTIAL would require, and consistent with (not merely trusting) TEST-RUNNER's Route 1 attribution of its own 16 observed failures. REQ-071 is genuinely done.
